'''Maria Colombo''' (born 25 May 1989){{r|cv}} is an Italian mathematician specializing in [[mathematical analysis]]. She is a professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) in Switzerland, where she holds the chair for mathematical analysis, [[calculus of variations]] and [[partial differential equation]]s.{{r|amcv|full}}

==Education and career==
Colombo was born in [[Luino]], near the Swiss border with Italy.{{r|cv|normale}} She competed for Italy in the 2005, 2006, and 2007 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]s, earning bronze, gold, and silver medals respectively.{{r|imo}}

She earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics at the [[University of Pisa]] in 2010 and 2011,{{r|cv}} and completed a PhD in 2015 at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]], under the joint supervision of [[Luigi Ambrosio]] and [[Alessio Figalli]].{{r|cv|mgp}} Her dissertation, ''Flows of non-smooth vector fields and degenerate elliptic equations: With applications to the Vlasov-Poisson and semigeostrophic systems'', was published as a book in 2017 by Edizioni della Normale.{{r|diss}}

She did postdoctoral research with [[Camillo De Lellis]] at the [[University of Zurich]] and was a junior fellow at the Institute of Theoretical Studies at [[ETH Zurich]]. She then joined the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] as an assistant professor in 2018,{{r|cv}} and was promoted to full professor in 2021.{{r|full}}

==Recognition==
The [[Accademia dei Lincei]] gave Colombo their Gioacchino Iapichino Prize for 2016.{{r|normale|iap}} She was the 2017 winner of the [[Carlo Miranda]] Prize of the {{ill|National Society of Sciences, Letters and Arts of Naples|it|Società Nazionale di Scienze, Lettere e Arti di Napoli}},{{r|normale|miranda}} and the 2019 winner of the [[Bartolozzi Prize]] of the [[Italian Mathematical Union]].{{r|bart}} She is the 2022 winner of the biennial Peter Lax Award, to be given at the International Conference on Hyperbolic Problems,{{r|lax}} and the 2023 winner of the Collatz Prize of the [[International Council for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], "for her fundamental contributions to regularity theory and the analysis of singularities in elliptic partial differential equations, geometric variational problems, transport equations, and incompressible fluid dynamics".{{r|collatz}} In 2024, she was awarded the [[EMS Prize]] for ''breakthrough results in fluid dynamics, optimal transport and kinetic theory, and for her impact on analysis more broadly''.{{r|ems}} That same year, she was awarded the [[Stampacchia Medal]].{{r|vf}}

==Personal life==
Colombo is married to an engineer, with whom she has four children.{{r|vf}}
